answer: At each epoch, agents bond collateral to a polynomial identity commitment—the anchor—and use private evaluations in RLN proofs. A proof shows tree membership and enforces a rate limit without exposing identity. Reusing a slot produces distinct Shamir shares; interpolation reveals the signing secret, enabling immediate slashing of the bond. Zero-knowledge proofs act as a prism for honest traffic, while a pearl-like commitment binds stake to one identity.
